column1: SigLA Linear A tablet texts rendered in Unicode
Actual tablet/document sign sequences derived from SigLA's scholarly sign-attestation
dataset, not a character inventory and not a translation. This snapshot was generated
2026-07-25 and contains 802 SigLA documents. SigLA reports that all Linear A
tablets listed in GORILA are present, plus selected other document types and newer finds.
Each row preserves the SigLA document identifier, metadata, sign order, approximate word
grouping, Unicode glyph sequence, scholarly display readings, GORILA sign identifiers,
The Unicode sequence is a derivative rendering: each classified SigLA GORILA sign ID was
mapped to its identically named Unicode 17.0 Linear A character. Uncertain readings retain
? in the ID/reading fields. [SIGN-ID] in the Unicode field marks an unclassified,
unreadable, or not-directly-encoded sign; it is deliberately not guessed. Spaces reflect
SigLA's word/role grouping, but line layout, two-dimensional placement, numerals not tagged
as sign attestations, erasures, damage, and palaeographic variants cannot be fully preserved
in plain text. Consult each source URL and drawing for the authoritative context. Linear A
is undeciphered; display readings are conventional approximate values, not translations.
Derived from SigLA: The Signs of Linear A, by Ester Salgarella and Simon Castellan.
SigLA dataset and drawings license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike
This transformed Unicode transcription is distributed under the same CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
license. Changes made: selected textual metadata/sign attestations, ordered occurrences,
mapped GORILA IDs to Unicode 17.0 code points, and serialized as UTF-8 TSV. No drawings or
INSCRIBE viewer (3D models; no direct alignment asserted here):
Tab-separated UTF-8. One record per document. A "-" value means SigLA did not supply it.
